value.title: Track attitudes after a fiscal-impact report is published
value.rationale: The source study's one-shot paragraph produced a small, imprecise shift; real fiscal information arriving in the news is the exposure that matters.
value.contribution: Moves the question from a framing paragraph to real-world information.
limitations: Timing of the report is not under the researcher's control.

data_sources: A rolling online panel (e.g. the Nationscape-style weekly surveys) with immigration attitude items
The publication dates of CBO immigration fiscal-impact reports
design.units: Panel respondents interviewed in the eight weeks around a report release.
design.exposure: Interview after versus before the release, and self-reported news exposure.
design.outcome: The same pro-immigration attitude index as the source study.
design.identification: Interrupted time series around the release date, with the prior year's same weeks as a control series.
threats: Other immigration news in the window
design.analysis_plan: OLS of the index on post-release, week-of-year and their interaction, HC2 standard errors; one pre-specified test of the post-release jump.
design.hypothesis: Attitudes move toward the report's conclusion in the weeks after its release.
